pins.definition: To say words aloud using the voice.
To say words aloud, have a conversation, or be able to use a language.
To use one's voice to produce words, converse, or use a language.

situation: A tour guide stands in front of a group at a museum, mid-sentence with his mouth open.
subject: the act of saying words aloud
brief: A man stands before a crowd in a gallery, his mouth open mid-syllable with visible breath rising from his lips, while the people around him listen attentively. The figure and speech are the absolute focus against a flat, brightly coloured background.
prompt: A man stands before a crowd in a gallery, his mouth open mid-syllable with visible breath rising from his lips, while the people around him listen attentively. The figure and speech are the absolute focus against a flat, brightly coloured background. a mid-century travel poster painted in gouache, rich opaque colour, confident simplified forms with real painted texture, strong diagonal composition. One square illustration. The scene is fully rendered and fully inhabited — no silhouettes, no flat icons, no diagram, no empty schematic space. A single subject dominates the frame and everything else is arranged around it. Absolutely no text anywhere in the image: no letters, words, numbers, captions, labels, signage, logos, watermarks or pseudo-text.
